To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The cell-binding domain of fibronectin, which contains an Arg-Gly-Asp-Sec sequence (RGDS) and mediates cell adhesion, can be separated from the heparin-binding site of the protein, which is also involved in cell adhesion.

the cell-binding activity of a fibronectin fragment is dependent upon its conformation and that the conformation of the cell-binding activity in the alpha- and gamma-chains of fibronectin is different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which cells interact with extracellular matrix (ECM) components and how these interactions affect cell behavior.
the role of the RGDS sequence in cell adhesion and neurite outgrowth and with the role of heparan sulfate proteoglycan in these responses.
the role of extracellular matrix in the regulation of neuronal cell adhesion and neurite extension, with particular emphasis on the fibronectin molecule.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a cell-binding domain in the f110 fragment of pFN that is not RGSD-dependent and is not dependent on heparin or heparan sulfates.
the cell binding domain of the fibronectin is the RGD sequence and that this sequence is the only one that is required for the binding of fibronectin to cells.
the RGDS sequence of the alpha-subunit of plasma FN is not required for the attachment or neurite outgrowth of human neuroblastomas on FN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the matrix adhesive responses of the LaN1 and Platt neuroblastoma cells are modulated by the sequences present in the fibronctins.

the matrix adhesive responses of cells are modulated by sequences that are not necessarily covalently linked but that are in a specific configuration and that the RGDS-dependent and heparan sulfate (HS)-dependent domains are not necessarily linked.
we have identified two cell-binding domains on the fibronectin molecule, one that is RGDS-dependent and the other that is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the matrix environment can modulate cell responses, and that this can be done by a variety of mechanisms.
the RGDS sequence is not sufficient to explain cell attachment to FN.
there is more than one mechanism of adhesion to fibronectin.
